raw_segments.text: Happier, had it sufficed him to have known good by itself, and evil not at all.
He sorrows now, repents and prays contrite, my motions in him.
Longer than they move, his heart I know, how variable and vain, self-left.
Lest therefore his now bolder hand reach also of the tree of life, and eat and live forever,
dream at least to live forever, to remove him I decree, and send him from the garden
forth to till the ground whence he was taken, fitter soil.
